PRIMARY.name: MEASUREMENT_BOUNDARY_DIFFERENCE
PRIMARY.explanation: Phase 12 used KV cache (--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v f16) which allows KV retrieval on subsequent tokens. This makes the inference baseline slower to measure (more computation = more time, so speedup denominator is inflated). Phase 13 measures fresh inference without KV cache reuse. In Phase 12: if native with cache is still faster than PRT with cache, PRT might show speedup because the cache retrieval path is the same for both — but PRT's FFN_UP is bypassed for cached tokens. In Phase 13: no cache means every token is computed fresh, so PRT's actual computation overhead is visible.
PRIMARY.evidence: Phase 12 explicitly used --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v f16. Phase 13 never used cache flags.
PRIMARY.counter_evidence: Phase 12 showed ~1.8x speedup even for first token (prompt evaluation) which shouldn't benefit from cache. But KV cache may have been partially populated from earlier prompt tokens.
PRIMARY.severity: This alone explains most of the discrepancy

SECONDARY.name: FRONTEND_BASELINE_DIFFERENCE
SECONDARY.explanation: Phase 12 used llama-prt-posix (built May 5) while Phase 13 uses llama-cli (built May 7). These are different binaries. llama-prt-posix may have had different optimization levels, different threading, or different graph compilation paths that changed the PRT compute cost vs native baseline ratio.
SECONDARY.evidence: Different binary filenames; different build timestamps; Phase 12 branch is a separate fork
SECONDARY.counter_evidence: Both binaries link against libllama.so which was rebuilt. But the binary that runs inference controls threading, batch scheduling, and loop structure.
SECONDARY.severity: May contribute but unlikely to flip 1.8x speedup to 2.5x slowdown alone

TERTIARY_A.name: PROMPT_SUITE_DIFFERENCE
TERTIARY_A.explanation: Phase 12 used 24 diverse prompts. Phase 13 AI used 'The capital of France is' repeated. Prompt complexity affects how much PRT computation is needed and whether KV cache effects matter.
TERTIARY_A.counter_evidence: Phase 13AF (5×5 timing) used the same prompt and still showed ~4.8x slowdown

TERTIARY_B.name: CODEPATH_DIFFERENCE
TERTIARY_B.explanation: Phase 12 PRT graph replacement and Phase 13 PRT graph replacement are very similar (both use build_prt_ffn_up and prt_ffn_up_custom_op). The kernel logic is nearly identical. The main code difference is Phase 13 added timing instrumentation and mmap loading. These shouldn't change compute speed by 4x.
TERTIARY_B.evidence: diff of prt_graph_replace.h between bca5a1f32 and current HEAD shows mostly timing additions; kernel logic identical
TERTIARY_B.counter_evidence: The kernel math is identical; timing code doesn't execute in hot path when log level is quiet

TERTIARY_C.name: PHASE 12 MAY HAVE BEEN MEASURING A SPECIFIC SCENARIO
TERTIARY_C.explanation: Phase 12 showed speedup for L12+L15 anchored PRT vs native. The anchor layers (11 and 15) are forced native. For the 34 PRT layers, the PRT custom op bypasses the FFN_UP entirely. If native FFN_UP on these layers is slower than PRT's sparse ternary matmul, then PRT wins. But in Phase 13, the same logic should apply — yet PRT is slower. This suggests the native baseline in Phase 12 was somehow slower (e.g., different model loading, different compute path) OR Phase 12 was measuring something other than end-to-end inference speed.
TERTIARY_C.evidence: Phase 12 showed 1.8x speedup with same L11+L15 policy
TERTIARY_C.counter_evidence: Phase 13AE quality suite confirms PRT produces valid output; the replacement is real. The 1.8x speedup is inconsistent with Phase 13's clean measurement.
TERTIARY_C.severity: Phase 12 result not reproducible with current stack; requires controlled rerun to resolve

TERTIARY_D.name: COUNTER_LOGGING_DIFFERENCE
TERTIARY_D.explanation: Phase 12 used 11BD counters (callback_overwrites, identity_fallback_calls). Phase 13 uses 13V-TIMING (kern_total, first_ms). These measure different things — Phase 12 counter shows 16 native_fallback_calls per token for anchored layers, while Phase 13 shows 0 fallback. This is because Phase 13 logs show only AVX2 active calls; Phase 12's 16/token is for layers 11 and 15 (2 layers × 8 tokens/batch = 16).
TERTIARY_D.evidence: Phase 12 documented 16 native_fallback_calls per token; Phase 13 shows 0 fallback
TERTIARY_D.counter_evidence: Phase 13's 0 fallback means no fallback happened — which is consistent since L11+L15 anchors layers 11 and 15 to native, not that no native computation was done
TERTIARY_D.severity: Measurement system difference, not a real discrepancy

verdict_explanation: Phase 12 showed ~1.8x speedup because it measured PRT with KV cache (q8_0/f16) active, which inflates the native baseline's computation time and makes PRT's bypass appear as a larger speedup. Phase 13 measures fresh inference without KV cache, where the native baseline is faster per token and PRT's sparse matmul overhead is fully visible. The two results are not comparable without accounting for the KV cache confounder.
